citation.title: Feedback control of stored energy and rotation with variable beam energy and perveance on DIII-D
citation.authors: M.D. Boyer, K.G. Erickson, B.A. Grierson, D.C. Pace, J.T. Scoville, J. Rauch, B.J. Crowley, J.R. Ferron, S.R. Haskey, D.A. Humphreys, R. Johnson, R. Nazikian, C. Pawley

topic: Feedback control of stored energy and toroidal rotation on DIII-D using variable neutral-beam voltage and perveance
own_question: Can the new in-shot beam voltage and perveance variation be used for model-based MIMO feedback control of power, torque, stored energy and rotation without beam modulation?
actual_method_and_evidence: Observer with disturbance estimation, steady-state and transient box-constrained QP, and lag compensation for beam current. Demonstrated on a few DIII-D shots. Rotation feedback used a single real-time impurity CER channel. The paper notes that beam modulation can reduce the availability of reliable CER measurements. No temperature nowcasting, no BES/ECEI inputs and no KSTAR data.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Real-time impurity charge-exchange rotation measurements have been used as feedback signals in DIII-D beam control, with measurement rate tied to the duty cycle of the viewed beam.
claim_checks.qualification: The signal was rotation, not Ti. Arrival timing was not quantified, and the work concerns DIII-D, not KSTAR.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Single CER channel fitted in real time. Update rate depends on beam duty cycle. No report latency was measured.
validation_if_relevant: Experimental demonstration shots only. No held-out predictive validation.
forbidden_inferences: Does not show that CES Ti nowcasting improves control
Does not concern electron diagnostics, BES or ECEI
Not evidence on main-ion versus impurity Ti
Do not generalize to KSTAR or to all prior work
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include only as an optional, brief application-context citation showing that CER-derived quantities feed real-time control. It is not needed for the core nowcasting framing.
